newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: TREASURER COY ON GST
Federal Treasurer, Peter Costello, is still not saying how much the income tax rate could be reduced if a Goods and Services Tax was introduced.
In an interview on Sydney radio 2UE, Mr Costello wouldn't directly say he personally supported a GST, instead saying the indirect tax-base needed to be broadened.
Mr Costello says if a proposal for tax reform is put up, the tax rates would have to be named.
"It's far too early at this stage to even talk about the introduction of something which was on all goods and all services," Mr Costello said.
"What we are doing is we are opening the lines for discussion. If you came up with a particular proposal you would of course name the trade-offs in relation to income tax," he said.
SNOWY RIVER GROUP DENIES MAKING BOMB THREAT
In the Snowy Mountains, the group campaigning for a return of water flows to the Snowy River has denied that it's behind a bomb threat to blow up one of the big hydro-electric water storages.
Security has been tightened around the Jindabyne Dam following the threat and the Snowy Mountains Hydro-electric Authority says it's blocked off vehicle access to the dam wall.

The Jindabyne Dam holds back water from the Snowy River, allowing it to be diverted for electricity generation and it's been the centre of a long-running dispute by landholders along the river who want some of the flow restored.
However, Paul Leete from the Snowy River Alliance says his group wouldn't want to see the dam wrecked.
NEW DEVICE GIVES DRUGS WITHOUT INJECTION
Brisbane researchers have uncovered a revolutionary device which delivers drugs into the skin without the need for injection.
The device is being used to give local anaesthetics to small areas of skin for routine procedures.
The electrical device is designed to reduce pain and the speed of anaesthetic or catheter insertion.
It uses a small electric current to deliver anaesthesia across the skin and into the bloodstream but without breaking the skin.
Clinical trials are currently underway on a number of volunteers at the Princess Alexandra Hospital.
If successful, this relatively cheap device may be used in routine procedures and the needle could become a thing of the past.
CAR IN MISSING TODDLER INQUIRY VANDALISED
In Victoria's Gippsland region, the car belonging to the last known person to see missing Moe toddler, Jaiden Leskie, alive, has been severely vandalised overnight.
Greg Domaszewicz's XE Falcon has been spray painted with the words "murderer" and "sinner" in red and white.
Jehovahs Witness magazines have been placed under the windscreen wipers.
The vacant block beside Mr Domaszewicz's house is littered with spray paint cans and the grass has been chewed up with tyre marks.
Police are at the house today talking to Mr Domaszewicz and Jaidyn's mother Belinda Murphy.
The search for baby Jaidyn has now reached its 19th day.
CLAIM OSTRICH DEATH WAS CAUSED BY BALLOONISTS
An ostrich valued at $23,000 has died, after its owners claim it was frightened by competitors in the Mildura International Balloon Fiesta, in north western Victoria.
The bird's owner, Larry Dimasi, says the ostrich died after being spooked by the balloons and running into a fence yesterday.
He says the balloon pilots don't make enough effort to stay well clear of the birds.
Mr Dimasi says the ostrich was one of his best cock-birds and he's considering legal action to recoup his losses.
He says while considerable effort has been put into liaising between ostrich owners and Fiesta organisers to prevent birds being spooked by the flights, it's not working.
He says a remark that there are about 40 farmers in the district and only two or three complaints have been made, is not good enough.
"I've lost a big investment and I reckon if they're going to sit back and say two or three complaints, that's not bad out of 40, they've got another think coming," Mr Dimasi said.
But the organisers of the Balloon Fiesta say they make every effort to ensure pilots avoid ostrich farms during the event.
Organiser Deidre Blackmore says all pilots are issued with a map marking the sensitive zones to avoid.
She says if it looks as if the balloons are heading in that direction organisers will call the ostrich farmers to warn them they might need to take action like starting tractors near the birds.
GAINSFORD-TAYLER WINS 200 METRES IN SWITZERLAND
Australian sprint star Melinda Gainsford-Taylor has beaten Olympic champion Marie-Jose Perec of France in the 200 metres event at the Grand Prix athletics meeting in Lausanne, Switzerland.
Gainsford-Taylor took the lead in the straight and held off a late challenge from Perec to win by three one-hundredths of a second.
In the men's 200 metres, Australia's Steve Brimacombe finished seventh behind Olympic silver medallist Ato Boldon of Trinidad.
And the men's 100 metres was won by American Maurice Greene ahead of Frankie Fredericks with world and Olympic champion Donovan Bailey in third place.
